name: chakrashri-backend
description: Production backend API for Chakrashri e-commerce (sacred objects, puja booking, astrology consultations)

scripts.//snapshot: Writes catalog.json — the build-time catalog the storefront renders its first paint from while the Render free-tier API is still waking (30-60s). Netlify runs this on every deploy. Run it by hand and COMMIT the result too: on a build where the API never wakes, the script refuses to publish an empty shop and keeps whatever copy is in the repo, so the committed one is the safety net.
scripts.//prerender: Writes product/<slug>/index.html for every product, so link-preview crawlers (WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter, Slack) — which never run JavaScript — get that product's real title, description, image and Product JSON-LD instead of the generic site head. Reads catalog.json, so run `npm run snapshot` first. Output is gitignored build artifact; Netlify regenerates it on every deploy.
scripts.//check:storefront: Answers 'did the snapshot capture everything, and do shared links show the right thing?'. Reads catalog.json and product/ and reports what a visitor would actually get. Read-only, no network. `check:share` does the same plus fetches the LIVE site to confirm the deploy actually ran the prerender step. Both exist as npm scripts rather than node -e one-liners because PowerShell strips the inner quotes of those and they fail before telling you anything.
scripts.//health: Answers 'is anything still keeping the API awake?'. Measures /api/health latency: a warm Render instance answers in under a second, one that has spun down takes 30-60s to boot, so a slow reply means the cron-job.org schedule has stopped. No credentials needed. The Keep-alive watch workflow runs this weekly and fails loudly, so you do not have to remember to check.
scripts.//catalog:drift: Answers 'is what visitors see still what the shop actually sells?'. Compares the live catalog against the catalog.json currently deployed and reports whether they differ. Read-only and safe to run any time. The scheduled workflow runs the same script WITHOUT --dry-run, which triggers a Netlify rebuild when they have drifted.
scripts.//test:drawer: Runs the REAL drawer renderer and category ranking over ~20 generated catalogues — empty, adversarial category names, and a 40x12 catalogue that does not exist yet. Needs nothing external. It is the only thing checking that 'top 15 by most sold' is a TOTAL order rather than whatever the sort happened to return.
scripts.//jobs: Free-plan only. The three cron services in render.yaml do not exist on Render's free tier; an external scheduler calls an HTTP trigger instead. `jobs:status` answers 'is the schedule actually firing?' and exits non-zero if no run has ever happened. `jobs:run` starts one immediately. Both read JOBS_TRIGGER_TOKEN from .env — the same value set in the Render dashboard — and never print it.
scripts.//email:log: Reads email_log to answer 'why did that email not arrive?'. Read-only. `npm run email:log -- --failed` shows only the ones that did not go out, with the SMTP error. Recipient local-parts are masked; the domain is kept because that is what matters for diagnosis.
scripts.//test: Everything that runs with no external services. This is what CI gates on and what to run before every commit. The two browser suites (test:browser, test:browser-settings) need a Chromium binary that npm install does NOT fetch — run `npm run setup:browser` once per machine. Without it they skip (exit 0) and the chain continues; set REQUIRE_BROWSER_TESTS=true, as CI does, to turn that skip into a failure.
scripts.test: npm run check:syntax && npm run test:unit && npm run test:coupons && npm run test:http && npm run test:security && npm run test:frontend && npm run test:browser && npm run test:browser-settings && npm run test:drawer
scripts.//verify: The offline suite plus the integration tests and live connectivity checks. Two suites here CAN skip themselves: test:browser without a Chromium binary, and test:db-integration without a throwaway database. Both say so loudly, but a skip still leaves verify green — so this is the developer command, not the gate.
scripts.verify: npm run test && npm run test:db-integration && npm run test:db && npm run test:razorpay
scripts.//verify:full: The actual pre-deploy gate, and what CI runs. Identical to verify except nothing is allowed to skip: a missing browser or missing test database becomes a failure instead of a notice. Needs TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at a DISPOSABLE database (a Neon branch, or a local Postgres) — never production; these tests create and delete rows.
scripts.//emails: The emails that are not triggered by a request: restock alerts, booking reminders, abandoned-checkout recovery and the daily digest. Every job is idempotent, so a duplicate run sends nothing. Runs as a Render cron every 15 minutes.
